verified_against_binary: v2.36.3 closes the one gap left by v2.36.2's clarity pass. That pass put the preinstalled inventory into the package-install rule, then moved it out to resolve a duplication with the neighbouring 'ships a large preinstalled stack' rule -- leaving the rule that says 'Prefer what is preinstalled' with no statement of what is preinstalled, and no pointer to the adjacent rule that had the numbers. A reader checking the ten items found it. The rule now names the stack in its own first sentence (Python 3.10.12, ~149 packages, pandas/numpy/PIL/openpyxl), duplicating one clause across two adjacent rules on purpose: a rule a reader can act on without reading its neighbour is worth a repeated sentence. No fact, tier, caveat or evidence date changed.
note: Also worth recording for future passes: of the ten reader questions answered in v2.36.2, only three were fixed in the RULE heading; six were fixed in the detail beneath, so a reader scanning headings still meets the original wording. That is a deliberate limit of this format, not an oversight -- but it means heading text carries more weight than its length suggests.
